item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 070511
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Tue Oct 6 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Rachel, located several hundred miles west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico (EP92):
A broad area of low pressure located offshore of southern Mexico is
producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental
conditions appear favorable for gradual development, and a tropical
depression is expected to form within the next day or so while the
system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward. Regardless
of development, heavy rainfall is forecast across portions of
southern and southwestern Mexico over the next few days. Interests
along the coast of southwestern Mexico should monitor the progress
of this system. For additional information, including Gale Warnings,
see High Seas forecasts issued by the National Weather Service.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

South of Guatemala:
An area of low pressure is forecast to form south of the coast of
Guatemala early next week. Environmental conditions appear conducive
for some gradual development of this system thereafter while it
moves generally west-northwestward around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

&&
High Seas Forecasts issued by the National Weather Service
can be found under AWIPS header NFDHSFEPI, WMO header FZPN02
KWBC, and on the web at ocean.weather.gov/shtml/NFDHSFEPI.php

$$
Forecaster Evans/Papin

item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Wed Oct 07 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 070859
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  41
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM PDT Wed Oct 07 2026
 
...RACHEL HOLDS STEADY AS IT CONTINUES WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.6N 121.2W
ABOUT 740 MI...1195 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...80 MPH...130 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 7 MPH...11 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...979 MB...28.91 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located 
near latitude 20.6 North, longitude 121.2 West. Rachel is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 7 mph (11 km/h), and a generally west 
to west-northwestward motion is expected during the next couple of 
days. Rachel is then forecast to slow down before making a sharp 
turn to the northeast by the end of the week.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 80 mph (130 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual to steady weakening is forecast over the next few 
days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 979 mb (28.91 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Pierce/Gibbs

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 40
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Tue Oct 06 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 070235
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  40
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM PDT Tue Oct 06 2026

Convective coverage has expanded somewhat across Rachel's northern 
semicircle. However, the storm's deepest convection remains 
concentrated across its southern half, indicative of northeasterly 
shear entraining dry air into the northern portion of the cyclone. 
The subjective Dvorak Current Intensity estimate from TAFB was 
4.5/77 kt, while objective estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 70 to 
75 kt. Given these intensity estimates and very little change in the 
overall satellite presentation, the initial intensity is held at 70 
kt.
 
The initial motion was estimated at 285/5 kt. Rachel continues to
be steered by high pressure anchored over the western United States.
However, by the end of the week, a large mid- to upper-level trough
is forecast to approach from the northwest, causing Rachel to slow
down before turning sharply northeastward. The system should then
gain forward speed as it moves toward Baja California and southern
California. Little change was made to the latest NHC track forecast,
other than to adjust it slightly toward the HCCA guidance.

The environment ahead of Rachel is expected to remain hostile, 
defined by dry mid-level air and cooling SSTs. Once Rachel makes 
its forecasted turn to the northeast, vertical wind shear is 
expected to increase as well, driven heavily by the aforementioned 
trough. As a result, steady weakening is expected to continue, and 
Rachel is forecast to become post-tropical by Saturday. The latest 
NHC intensity forecast is essentially unchanged from the previous 
advisory.
